title: Standalone review squad
summary: A standalone review session MUST resolve one review target, capture it once, delegate a single review-squad coordinator over that capture, and end with one ranked finding set and a verdict without changing a file.
instructions: The session MUST resolve exactly one review target before it captures anything: a ref range, a pull request, or a ref range the operator narrowed to a named path set; the path set filters the capture and never replaces the range the scope check runs on. When the request names no target, the session MUST derive the range from the current branch against its merge base with the default branch and MUST state the range it chose. When the request is ambiguous rather than absent, the session MUST ask the operator instead of guessing.

The session MUST write the captured target to one file beside its governance card and MUST hand that path to the coordinator. A single capture is what keeps every dimension agent reading the same bytes; re-deriving the target per agent lets the review drift.

Before delegating, the session MUST bind the review workspace to the target's head commit and MUST tell the coordinator which path that is. A dimension agent confirms a finding by reading the code around it, so a workspace parked at another commit yields findings about files the capture never described. When the current checkout is not already at that head, the session MUST resolve a worktree from it rather than review against the wrong tree.

The session MUST run the harness review-scope check on the resolved target before it delegates, and MUST act on each reported conflict by its tier. An instrument conflict — the lineup, a charter, the coordinator, the mode policy, an entry point, the scope check, or the reviewer's model mapping — leaves the squad's verdict, goes to an independent reviewer that does not run the squad, and is named in the report, because a charter cannot find a defect introduced into that charter. A conduct conflict — a policy on the reviewer's own card or guidance it delivers — stays in the squad's scope, and the session MUST build its card with the base revision so its conduct follows the rule in force before the change. A substrate conflict — validation code, test helpers, check wrappers, the gate cache, an exemption registry, the changelog — stays in scope, and every finding whose verification leans on such a file MUST say so.

A change to a standard MUST NOT be rejected for differing from the standard it replaces. When the target changes a policy, the report MUST carry a standards delta naming each instruction the change removed and each it added, and the merits of that change belong to the operator as a decision distinct from the code that benefits from it. The squad judges whether the changed rule agrees with every surface it did not touch and whether an agent can execute it; it does not judge whether the new rule is better.

The intent brief MUST be derived by the coordinator from the target's own artifacts — commit subjects, the request, a linked card or acceptance criteria — and the session MUST supply those sources rather than the brief. Every finding dropped as already answered MUST quote the brief line that answers it, so the operator can audit the drops.

When the conversation running the session authored any part of the target, the session MUST disclose that in the report as a deviation and SHOULD hand the review to a fresh session. On a repeat review of the same target, dimension agents MUST produce their findings on the delta before they see the prior finding set, and the coordinator reconciles afterwards.

The session MUST delegate exactly one review-squad coordinator per review round, and that coordinator alone owns the lineup, the join, the ranking, and the verdict. A dimension agent the coordinator spawns is a nested spawn and runs on the platform default model, which is not acceptable for charter-scoped review work. The session MUST therefore issue the dimension fan-out itself, at the top level and in one message, using the charters, capture, workspace, and finding shape the coordinator resolved, and MUST hand the raw findings back to the same coordinator, naming any charter whose subagent could not start. The coordinator MAY apply such a charter itself in join mode and MUST record which charters it applied. The session MUST NOT join, rank, drop, or grade a finding itself.

The session MUST report which dimensions ran, which conditional dimensions the target did not activate, and which charters the coordinator applied itself because a subagent could not start. A dimension that returned nothing MUST appear as empty rather than be omitted.

Neither the session, nor the coordinator, nor any dimension agent, nor the independent reviewer the session delegates for the instrument tier MAY edit a file, stage a change, commit, push, or write workflow state. A standalone review yields findings only, and acting on them is a separate operator decision.

The session MUST close with one operator-facing report carrying the resolved target, the ranked findings in the squad finding shape, every dropped finding with the reason it was dropped, and a pass or fail verdict.

guidance_sources.read_trigger: Read this guidance before you resolve the lineup, delegate a charter, or judge a finding.
